items.stem: The speed of light in a medium is $2 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. What is the refractive index of the medium? (Given that the speed of light in vacuum = $3 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$)

When a light ray travels from air to water with an angle of incidence of $45^\circ$, the angle of refraction is $32.1^\circ$. What is the speed of light in the water? (Given that the speed of light in vacuum = $3 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$)
items.hint: By Snell's law, $n = \dfrac{\sin 45^\circ}{\sin 32.1^\circ} \approx 1.33$. Then $n = \dfrac{c}{v}$, so $v = \dfrac{c}{n} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}}{1.33} \approx 2.25 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

items.stem: A boy is looking at small print on a piece of paper. He moves a glass block of uniform thickness $3\ \text{cm}$ over the print. The print appears to rise by $0.9\ \text{cm}$. What is the refractive index of the glass?
items.hint: Apparent depth = real depth − rise = $3\ \text{cm} - 0.9\ \text{cm} = 2.1\ \text{cm}$. $n = \dfrac{\text{real depth}}{\text{apparent depth}} = \dfrac{3}{2.1} \approx 1.43$. Option A is $\dfrac{2.1}{3}$. Option D uses the rise instead of the apparent depth ($\dfrac{3}{0.9}$).
